subject: comparing models with first-order and second-order Markov processes

messages.author: 527d9b3ec7deff2d
messages.subject: comparing models with first-order and second-order Markov processes
parts:
Hi all,

I've got a multi-state model where we are exploring nth-order Markov processes for breeding site presence, given a breeding interval >2 yrs.  For example, a female with offspring could conceivably not return to the breeding site for 3 years, so the history of partially latent breeding site presences needs to go beyond t-1.  This is referred to as a "memory model" in MARK, though MARK cannot actually fit models beyond a first-order Markov process.  This is trivial in JAGS.

The problem I am having is with model comparison, as it is not clear which metrics can be used to compare models with a Markovian dependence that is first-order vs. second-order, etc.  I tried including the breeding interval as a random variable, but the chains get stuck at initial values and do not mix (unsurprisingly).  The problem is that the models condition on more and more latent states as you go up in order, so of course things like deviance are going to increase.

As it stands, the second-order model has the greatest separation between probabilities of breeding site presence for individuals that were present in years t-1 or t-2, and those that were not.  Maybe this is the best I can do...

Just curious if anyone has addressed this problem, particularly in the literature.  The issue should be the same for spatial CAR processes, so it would seem to be a fairly general problem.  Would be nice if there is something I've overlooked.

Thanks,
Dan
